1986), nicknamed "'''Big Al'''", is a Dominican professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He is a five-time [[NBA All-Star]] and an [[NBA champion]]. Horford played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]] and was the starting [[center (basketball)|center]] on their back-to-back [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) national championship teams in [[2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2006]] and [[2007 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2007]]. He was drafted with the third overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Atlanta Hawks]], with whom he played nine seasons before signing with the Celtics as a free agent in the 2016 offseason. After three seasons in Boston, Horford played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] and the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] before being traded back to the Celtics prior to the 2021 season. He reached the [[NBA Finals]] with the Celtics in [[2022 NBA Finals|2022]] and [[2024 NBA Finals|2024]], winning his first NBA title in 2024. ==Early life== Horford was born in [[Puerto Plata (city)|Puerto Plata]], Dominican Republic. His father, [[Tito Horford]], played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for three years and several more in other countries. In 2000, Horford and his family moved to [[Lansing, Michigan]], where he attended Grand Ledge High School in [[Grand Ledge, Michigan]], and was a star on its basketball team. Horford holds seven school records, including most career points (1,239). As a senior, he was named "Class A Player of the Year" after averaging 21 points, 13 rebounds, and five blocks per game. While at Grand Ledge, Horford played [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball for the Michigan Mustangs, who were runners-up in the Adidas Big Time National Tournament.{{cite web|url=http://horford15.com/personal |title=Personal |work=Horford15.com |access-date=January 27, 2012 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110417050652/http://horford15.com/personal |archive-date=April 17, 2011 }} Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], he was listed as the No. 7 power forward and the No. 36 player in the nation in 2004.{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/19938|title=Al Horford|work=Rivals.com|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=July 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160702151504/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/19938|url-status=live}} ==College career== Horford accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]], choosing the Gators over [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], and [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]].{{Cite web |title=Al Horford Recruit Interests |url=https://247sports.com/Recruitment/Al-Horford-69905/RecruitInterests/ |access-date=2022-06-04 |website=247sports.com}} There, he played for coach [[Billy Donovan]] and teamed up alongside [[Joakim Noah]], [[Corey Brewer]] and [[Taurean Green]]. Horford made an immediate impact for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Gators]] in [[2004–05 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2004–05]], starting at center in the front court with [[David Lee (basketball)|David Lee]], and helped the Gators win the [[2005 SEC men's basketball tournament|2005 Southeastern Conference tournament]] championship. The Gators surged through the 2005–06 season, winning the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] championship for a second straight year. They entered the [[2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2006 NCAA tournament]] as the No. 3 seed. The Gators swept through the first four rounds to reach the [[Final Four]], then defeated [[Underdog|Cinderella]] team [[2005–06 George Mason Patriots men's basketball team|George Mason]] to reach the [[2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|championship game]], where they defeated [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] for the school's first national title behind Horford's 14 points and seven rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=264000063|title=Gators clamp down on UCLA to win first NCAA title|publisher=ESPN|date=April 3, 2006|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=April 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160409204302/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=264000063|url-status=dead}} [[Image:Al Horford.jpg|thumb|left|Horford with Florida as a junior]] In December 2006, midway through his junior year, Horford missed a series of games due to injury. Coach Donovan held him out of a game against [[Stetson Hatters men's basketball|Stetson]] in hopes that he would be adequately healed for a game in Gainesville against the third-ranked [[2006–07 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State Buckeyes]] on December 23. Though Donovan had previously announced that Horford would be unable to play, Horford entered the game from the bench to guard Ohio State's star freshman [[Greg Oden]], holding him to seven points, well below his season average of 15. Horford recorded 11 points and 11 rebounds in limited action as the Gators defeated the Buckeyes. On March 4, 2007, in the final home game of the season against [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], he became the fourth player on his team to score 1,000 career points, scoring exactly the required 14 points to reach the milestone.{{cite web|last=Brockway|first=Kevin|url=http://www.gainesville.com/news/20070304/uf-rebounds-with-record-win-over-kentucky|title=UF rebounds with record win over Kentucky|work=Gainesville.com|date=March 4, 2007|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=July 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160709122323/http://www.gainesville.com/news/20070304/uf-rebounds-with-record-win-over-kentucky|url-status=live}} On April 2, 2007, the Gators [[2007 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|repeated as national champions]], becoming the first team to do so since the 1991–92 [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], and the first ever to do so with the same starting lineup (Horford, Noah, Brewer, Green, and [[Lee Humphrey]]). They defeated Oden and [[Mike Conley Jr.]] in a rematch of the regular season, by a score of Gators 84, Buckeyes 75.{{Cite news |last=Vecsey |first=George |date=2007-04-03 |title=Two Star Players, Two Glimpses of the College Experience |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/04/03/sports/ncaabasketball/03vecsey.html |access-date=2022-06-04 |issn=0362-4331}} Three days later, Horford, Noah, Brewer, and Green all declared for the [[NBA draft]].{{cite web|last=Katz|first=Andy|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2827116|title=Florida's four juniors to enter NBA draft|publisher=ESPN|date=April 5, 2007|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=January 15, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160115030831/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2827116|url-status=live}} ==Professional career== ===Atlanta Hawks (2007–2016)=== ====All-Rookie honors (2007–2008)==== On June 28, 2007, Horford was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the third overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/2007_Draft_Central.html |title=Hawks Take Al Horford At No. 3; Acie Law At No. 11 |work=NBA.com |access-date=July 9, 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080115053712/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/2007_Draft_Central.html |archive-date=January 15, 2008 }} On July 9, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Hawks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2007_08/|title=Transactions: 2007-08 Season|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=May 31, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150531052916/http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2007_08/|url-status=live}} As a rookie in [[2007–08 Atlanta Hawks season|2007–08]], Horford was the only player unanimously selected to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]]; he was also runner-up for Rookie of the Year honors and was named Rookie of the Month on four occasions. Horford became the first Atlanta draftee to earn first team honors since [[Stacey Augmon]] in 1991–92.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/al_horford/bio/|title=Al Horford Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160708190015/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/al_horford/bio/|archive-date=July 8, 2016|url-status=dead}} Horford averaged 10.1 points, 9.7 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 0.9 blocks, 0.7 steals and 31.4 minutes in 81 games (77 starts). The Hawks finished the regular season with a 37–45 record and entered the playoffs as the eighth seed in the Eastern Conference. In their first round match-up with the [[Boston Celtics]], Horford helped the Hawks take the eventual champions to seven games, losing the series 4–3. In the series, Horford averaged 12.6 points and 10.4 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/horfoal01/gamelog/2008/|title=Al Horford 2007-08 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=July 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160704080811/http://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/horfoal01/gamelog/2008/|url-status=live}} ====Back-to-back All-Star selections (2008–2011)==== [[File:Al Horford2.jpg|thumb|Horford in 2008]] In [[2008–09 Atlanta Hawks season|2008–09]], Horford started all 67 games he played, averaging 11.5 points, 9.3 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 1.4 blocks and 0.8 steals in 33.5 minutes.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/horfoal01/gamelog/2009/|title=Al Horford 2008-09 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=July 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160704080031/http://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/horfoal01/gamelog/2009/|url-status=live}} With a 47–35 record, the Hawks entered the playoffs as the fourth seed in the East. Horford helped the Hawks advance to the second round where they were swept by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]; Horford missed Game 2 of the series due to injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290507005|title=Cavs remain unbeaten in 2009 playoffs behind James' 27 points in three quarters|publisher=ESPN|date=May 7, 2009|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=December 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141224182703/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290507005|url-status=dead}} Horford had an outstanding season in [[2009–10 Atlanta Hawks season|2009–10]], becoming the first Hawks draft pick to earn an All-Star berth since [[Kevin Willis]] did so in 1992. Horford contributed 14.2 points, 9.9 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.1 blocks and 0.7 steals in 35.1 minutes (.551 FG%, .789 FT%), appearing in 81 games. He ranked eighth in the NBA in field goal percentage, 10th in rebounds, tied for ninth in offensive rebounds (2.9), and 26th in blocks. Horford had a team-leading 39 double-doubles, which was tied for 11th in the NBA. Playing alongside [[Mike Bibby]], [[Jamal Crawford]], [[Joe Johnson (basketball)|Joe Johnson]], [[Josh Smith]] and [[Marvin Williams]], the Hawks entered the playoffs as the third seed in the East with a 53–29 record. 24, 2018|url-status=live}} In 77 games in [[2010–11 Atlanta Hawks season|2010–11]], Horford posted averages of 15.3 points, 9.3 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 1.0 blocks and 0.8 steals (.557 FG%, .500 3FG%, .798 FT%). He ranked fifth in the NBA in field goal percentage, 28th in blocks and 16th in efficiency (22.5). Horford was also one of the top all-around rebounders in the league, finishing 11th in rebounds, seventh in defensive rebounds (7.0) and tied for 24th in offensive rebounds (2.4). He had 36 double-doubles (tied for ninth in NBA), including one 20/20 game. He was named [[All-NBA Team|Third-Team All-NBA]]. With a 44–38 record, the Hawks entered the playoffs as the fifth seed in the East. They reached the second round again, where they lost 4–2 to the [[Chicago Bulls]]. ====Injury-shortened season (2011–2012)==== Due to the [[2011 NBA lockout]], the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]] did not begin until December 25, 2011. Horford appeared in the Hawks' first 11 games of the season before missing the final 55 due to a torn left pectoral muscle, an injury suffered on January 11, 2012, against the [[Indiana Pacers]]. Six days later, he underwent surgery to repair the muscle and was ruled out for three to four months.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7472272/al-horford-atlanta-hawks-undergoes-successful-surgery-pectoral-muscle|title=Al Horford has successful surgery|publisher=ESPN|date=January 17, 2012|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=February 25, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220225170628/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7472272/al-horford-atlanta-hawks-undergoes-successful-surgery-pectoral-muscle|url-status=live}} With a 40–26 record, the Hawks entered the playoffs as the fifth seed in the East. Horford missed an additional three playoff games before returning to action in Game 4 of the Hawks' first round series against the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20120506/ATLBOS/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Celtics 101, Hawks 79|publisher=ESPN|date=May 6, 2012|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190710153341/https://www.nba.com/games/20120506/ATLBOS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=July 10, 2019|url-status=dead}} He played out the series, which the Hawks lost in six games. ====Career-best season (2012–2013)==== In the [[2012–13 Atlanta Hawks season|2012–13 season]], Horford started all 74 games he played, averaging a career-high 17.4 points, career-high 10.2 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.1 blocks and career-high 1.1 steals in 37.2 minutes. He recorded 43 double-doubles (20 20-point/10-rebound games), including one in points and assists. Horford scored 20-plus points in nine consecutive games (February 11 – March 3) for the first time in his career. On November 26, 2012, Horford was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week for the first time in his career.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/al-horford-named-eastern-conference-player-week|title=HORFORD WINS EASTERN PLAYER OF THE WEEK HONORS|work=NBA.com|date=November 26, 2012|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=September 11, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160911185351/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/al-horford-named-eastern-conference-player-week|url-status=live}} On February 27, 2013, Horford scored a career-high 34 points in a 102–91 victory over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130227/ATLUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Hawks 102, Jazz 91|work=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2012|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160911065351/http://www.nba.com/games/20130227/ATLUTA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=September 11, 2016|url-status=dead}} With a 44–38 record, the Hawks entered the playoffs as the sixth seed in the East. In their first round match-up against the [[Indiana Pacers]], the Hawks were defeated 4–2 despite a playoff career-high 16.7 points per game from Horford over the six games.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/horfoal01/gamelog/2013/|title=Al Horford 2012-13 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=July 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160704080816/http://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/horfoal01/gamelog/2013/|url-status=live}} ====Second injury-shortened season (2013–2014)==== [[File:Al Horford Nov 2013.jpg|thumb|Horford in 2013]] Over the first 29 games of the [[2013–14 Atlanta Hawks season|2013–14 season]], Horford posted nine double-doubles and scored in double-figures 28 times, including 13 20-point outings and one 30-point game. Over this stretch, he averaged a career-best 18.6 points per game. However, another shoulder injury suffered on December 26, 2013, sidelined Horford for the rest of the season. Initially considered a "bruised right shoulder",{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131226/ATLCLE/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Hawks 127, Cavs 125 2OT|work=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2013|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160718065104/http://www.nba.com/games/20131226/ATLCLE/gameinfo.html|archive-date=July 18, 2016|url-status=dead}} the injury turned out to be a complete tear of his right pectoral muscle,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-injury-report-december-27-2013|title=HAWKS INJURY REPORT – DECEMBER 27, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2013|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=February 4, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150204124558/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-injury-report-december-27-2013|url-status=live}} and required season-ending surgery.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/12/31/al-horford-surgery-hawks.ap/|title=Hawks' Horford has season-ending surgery|work=NBA.com|date=December 31, 2013|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151030021402/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/12/31/al-horford-surgery-hawks.ap/|archive-date=October 30, 2015|url-status=dead}} Horford did not play in the postseason, where the Hawks lost in the first round to the [[Indiana Pacers]]. ====Return to All-Star form (2014–2016)==== In [[2014–15 Atlanta Hawks season|2014–15]], Horford played in 76 regular season games, the most since the 2010–11 season.
